title: Cut materials using the oxy-fuel gas cutting process (manual cutting)

lessons.title: How oxy-fuel cutting works and its hazards
lessons.html:
The oxy-fuel cutting process

Oxy-fuel cutting uses a flame of fuel gas (usually acetylene, sometimes LPG) mixed with oxygen to heat steel to its ignition temperature, a bright red colour. A jet of pure oxygen is then blown onto the hot spot. The steel burns (oxidises) and the jet blows the molten oxide away, leaving a cut called the kerf. In farm workshops it is used to cut plate, beams, scrap and rusted bolts.

Oxy-fuel cutting works well on mild and low-carbon steel. It does not cut stainless steel, aluminium, copper or cast iron properly.

Equipment

  • Oxygen cylinder (usually black in South Africa) and fuel gas cylinder (acetylene usually maroon). Always read the cylinder label to confirm contents rather than relying on colour alone.
  • Regulators for each gas, with contents and working pressure gauges.
  • Flashback arrestors fitted at the regulators, and non-return valves at the torch.
  • Hoses: oxygen hose and fuel hose with different colours and threads. Fuel gas fittings normally have left-hand threads.
  • Cutting torch with a cutting oxygen lever and the correct size cutting nozzle.
  • Spark lighter, nozzle cleaners and a trolley with a chain to secure cylinders.

Hazards

  • Fire and explosion: sparks and molten slag can travel several metres and start fires.
  • Flashback: the flame burns back into the torch or hoses. It can cause an explosion.
  • Oxygen and oil: oil or grease in contact with high-pressure oxygen can ignite violently. Never oil regulators or fittings, and do not handle them with greasy hands.
  • Burns from hot metal, slag and the flame.
  • Eye damage from glare and flying slag.
  • Fumes, especially from painted, galvanised or coated metal.
  • Cylinder hazards: a falling cylinder can break its valve and become a dangerous projectile.

lessons.title: Safe set-up and lighting
lessons.html:
Preparing the work area

  • Remove flammable materials such as fuel, oil, rags, dry grass and chaff from the area, or cover them with fire blankets.
  • Never cut containers, tanks or drums that held fuel, oil or chemicals unless they have been made safe by a competent person.
  • Have a fire extinguisher ready.
  • Ensure good ventilation.
  • Put the work on a cutting table or firm support so the cut-off piece falls safely and not onto your feet or the hoses.

PPE

  • Gas welding or cutting goggles or face shield with the correct shade lens
  • Leather gloves
  • Flame-resistant overalls with no open pockets or turn-ups
  • Leather apron and spats
  • Safety boots

Setting up the equipment

  1. Secure cylinders upright on the trolley with a chain.
  2. Check that regulators, hoses, flashback arrestors and torch are in good condition. Replace damaged hoses; do not tape them.
  3. Fit the correct nozzle size for the thickness of metal, according to the nozzle chart.
  4. Open cylinder valves slowly. Stand to the side of the regulator, not in front of it.
  5. Set the working pressures given in the manufacturer's chart for the nozzle.
  6. Leak-test all connections with a leak detection solution or soapy water. Bubbles show a leak. Never use a flame to test for leaks.
  7. Purge each hose briefly to remove any mixed gases.

Lighting the torch

Follow the lighting sequence given by your equipment maker and workplace procedure. A common sequence is:

  1. Open the fuel valve on the torch slightly and light with a spark lighter, never a match or cigarette lighter.
  2. Increase fuel until the flame stops smoking.
  3. Slowly open the preheat oxygen valve until you have a neutral flame: small, sharp, light-blue inner cones with no feathery tip.
  4. Press the cutting oxygen lever and readjust to neutral if needed.

If the torch pops repeatedly (backfire) or you hear a hissing or squealing sound inside the torch (flashback), shut off the gases immediately at the torch and then the cylinders, and report it.

lessons.title: Making the cut, shutting down and checking quality
lessons.html:
Cutting technique

  1. Mark the cut line clearly with soapstone or a scriber. Use a straight edge or guide for straight cuts.
  2. Hold the torch with both hands, comfortable and steady.
  3. Start at the edge of the plate. Hold the inner cones just above the surface at the distance recommended for the nozzle.
  4. Preheat until the spot is bright red.
  5. Slowly press the cutting oxygen lever. Sparks and slag should blow through the underside of the plate.
  6. Move steadily along the line at a constant speed and distance.
  7. At the end of the cut, release the cutting oxygen and lift the torch away.

Signs of a good or poor cut

AppearanceLikely cause
Square, smooth face, near-vertical drag lines, little slagCorrect speed, pressure and nozzle height
Heavy slag stuck underneathToo slow or too much preheat
Cut does not go through, sparks blow backToo fast or cutting oxygen pressure too low
Rounded, melted top edgeNozzle too close or too much preheat
Wide, uneven kerfUnsteady hand, dirty or damaged nozzle

Shutting down

Follow your equipment maker's shutdown sequence. Typically: close the torch valves in the specified order, close both cylinder valves, open the torch valves to bleed pressure from the hoses, then close them and wind out the regulator adjusting screws. Hang up the torch so the nozzle is not damaged.

After cutting

  • Mark hot pieces or let them cool before handling.
  • Chip off slag and grind the edge if needed. Wear eye protection.
  • Check the dimensions of the cut part.
  • Inspect the area for smouldering fires for a period after finishing.
  • Clean nozzles with the correct nozzle cleaner, not wire or drills that enlarge the hole.
  • Store cylinders upright, chained, with valves closed and caps fitted when moved.

Key points

  • Oxy-fuel cutting works on mild steel, not stainless steel, aluminium or cast iron.
  • Fit flashback arrestors and non-return valves; leak-test with soapy water.
  • Keep oil and grease away from oxygen equipment.
  • Clear flammables, chain cylinders upright and keep an extinguisher close.
  • Light with a spark lighter and adjust to a neutral flame.
  • Shut off immediately on flashback and report it.
